titleTr: Okul işleri: modal edilgen ve have/get something done

grammar.topic: Modal passive and have / get something done
explainTr: Modal edilgen: modal + be + V3. The roof must be repaired. (Çatı tamir edilmeli.) The projector can be fixed. (Projektör tamir edilebilir.) Yasak ve olasılık da aynı kalıpla verilir: Phones must not be used. The gym might be closed.

Have / get something done, işi başkasına yaptırmak demektir: I had my phone repaired. (Telefonumu tamir ettirdim.) The school gets the carpets cleaned every summer. 'Get' daha günlük konuşma dilidir. Kalıp: have/get + nesne + V3.
Aynı kalıp kötü olaylar için de kullanılır: She had her bag stolen. (Çantası çalındı.) Burada kişi işi yaptırmamıştır, başına gelmiştir; bağlamdan anlarsın.
grammar.compareTr: Türkçede 'yaptırmak' fiile eklenir (tamir ettirdim). İngilizcede ek yoktur: have + nesne + V3. 'Saçımı kestirdim' = I had my hair cut.
table: I have my car washed monthly.

reading.title: Room 9
reading.text:
On Tuesday morning, Hafsa walked into Room 9 and immediately looked up. A brown circle was spreading across the ceiling, and a bucket had been placed under it. "It leaks every time it rains," said Mr. Brown, who had come to show her around. "The roof must be repaired, but the district hasn't approved the money yet."

Hafsa noticed other problems. The projector was dead. The carpet near the door was torn. One window could not be opened. She felt sorry for the regular teacher, Ms. Park, who had asked for these repairs three times. "Can the projector be fixed?" Hafsa asked. "It should be," Mr. Brown said. "We had it checked last month, and the technician said it was faulty. The warranty ended in August, so we need an estimate first."

During recess Hafsa wrote a note for Ms. Park, as sub teachers often do. "The projector doesn't work, so I used the whiteboard. The ceiling should be inspected again, because the bucket was almost full." She also added a friendly line: "The students were wonderful. Leo cleaned the board without being asked."

At lunch she met the janitor, Mr. Okafor, a tall man with a big ring of keys. "You know, many of these things can be solved quickly," he said. "I fix what I can, but the big jobs need a contractor. The school has the roof inspected every year, but nobody wants to pay for a new one."

Hafsa thought about her own apartment. Last winter she had had her heater repaired twice, and her neighbor Linda had had the same problem. "Sometimes you have to ask more than once," she said. Mr. Okafor laughed. "Exactly. That's why I like your note. It's polite, but it's clear."

By the afternoon, the bucket had been emptied twice. When the final bell rang, Hafsa left her note on Ms. Park's desk, took a last look at the ceiling, and whispered, "Hang in there." She was not sure whether she was talking to the room or to herself.

listening.title: Repairs at home and at school

script.speaker: Linda
script.text: Hafsa, you won't believe my week. I had my kitchen ceiling repaired, and now the bathroom is leaking.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Oh no. Did you call the contractor again?

script.speaker: Linda
script.text: Yes. He's coming Thursday. I'm having new carpet installed in the hall, too.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Wow. You're having a lot done.

script.speaker: Linda
script.text: I know. The first estimate was too high, so I got a second one. The second contractor will do everything for six hundred dollars less.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: That's smart. Is there a warranty?

script.speaker: Linda
script.text: Two years. Everything must be inspected after the work is done.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: At school it's similar. A projector needs to be fixed, but the warranty has ended.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: The district. They're getting an estimate. It might be fixed by next month.

script.speaker: Linda
script.text: Well, at least you wrote a note.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Yes, and the janitor liked it. Now come over. I'll make tea while you tell me everything.

writing.promptTr: Müdüre ya da ön ofise resmi bir e-posta yaz: sınıfta gördüğün sorunları anlat ve tamir iste. Modal edilgen ve have/get something done kullan.
writing.promptEn: Write a formal email (120-180 words) to the front office about problems in a classroom. Use modal passive forms and at least one have/get something done structure.
frames: Dear Mr. Brown, I am writing about ...
The ... must be ... as soon as possible.
It would be helpful if the ... could be ...
Thank you for your help. Best regards, ...
writing.model: Dear Mr. Brown, I am writing about some problems in Room 9, where I substituted on Tuesday. First, there is a leak in the ceiling, and a bucket has been placed under it. I think the roof should be inspected as soon as possible, because the water might damage the carpet. Second, the projector is faulty and cannot be used. I understand that the warranty has ended, so perhaps an estimate could be requested from a contractor. It would also be helpful if one of the windows could be fixed, because it cannot be opened at all. I know that the school has had many repairs done this year, and I appreciate your hard work. I only want the students to have a safe and comfortable room. If you would like, I can write down the details for the maintenance team. Thank you very much for your time and your help. Best regards, Hafsa
checklistTr: En az iki modal edilgen cümle var mı (must be fixed, should be inspected)?
Bir have/get something done kalıbı kullandın mı?
Resmi bir giriş ve kapanış (Dear..., Best regards) var mı?
Cümleler büyük harfle başlıyor ve noktayla bitiyor mu?
